# Import a plain-text list of URLs into the library

## Intent

Alexandria is a personal, private library of web links for one person at a time. This package moves an existing pile of links into it in one step: the owner uploads a plain-text file of up to 5,000 URLs, every line is normalised and added as if it had been pasted, duplicates and malformed lines are reported rather than added, the order the owner gave the file is kept, and the imported links are fetched and enriched in the background at a pace that keeps the provider calls and the owner's costs low. Without it, the 600 open tabs that motivated the library would have to be pasted one by one.

## Goals

- A plain-text file of up to 5,000 URLs is imported in one upload, with duplicates reported rather than added.
- The owner sees counts of added, duplicate and invalid lines, the invalid lines with their line numbers, and can download the report.
- Imported links enter the stream in file order, the first line highest, with last used = the import time.
- Fetch and enrichment of imported links run in the background at no more than 20 links per minute per user, and the stream fills in as they complete.
- The import is available through the API with the same report returned as JSON.

## Non-goals

- Importing browser bookmark exports (the Netscape bookmark HTML format) or other structured formats; an HTML importer that keeps folder names as tags is a later PRD.
- Crawling beyond the page at each imported URL.
- Accounts, adding links, normalisation, the library limit and the stream: package 01 (`accounts_links_and_stream`), whose rules this reuses.
- Fetching and snapshots: package 02 (`fetch_and_snapshot`). Enrichment, the AI key and the shared background throttle: package 03 (`ai_enrichment`).
- Workspaces (04), decay and liveness (05), search (06), the MCP server (08), export and account deletion (09).
- Sharing or any cross-user feature; cross-user de-duplication of fetching.

## Background

After packages 01 to 03 the library has: users, sessions and tokens; `normalizeUrl` in `src/worker/links/normalize.ts`; the link store in `src/worker/links/store.ts`, which adds a pending link or boosts an existing one, and `POST /api/v1/links/batch`, which gives a batch descending last-used times so that its first URL ends highest; the 20,000-link library limit (409 `library_full`); the stream at `GET /api/v1/links`; the error envelope and the OpenAPI document that a test keeps in step with the routes; the fetch worker (`src/worker/fetcher/`, fed by the `FETCH_QUEUE` Queue) that fetches, snapshots and moves a link out of `pending`, with the website updating the stream in place as links change; enrichment (`src/worker/enrich/`), which runs after a successful fetch when the user has an AI key; and the shared background throttle `src/worker/enrich/throttle.ts`, at most 20 links per minute per user, used by "enrich all unenriched links". The settings page (`src/web/pages/Settings.tsx`) holds the tokens and the AI key. There is no import.

Constraints from the source PRD:

- Constraint: TypeScript; API in Hono on Cloudflare Workers; data in D1; background work on Cloudflare Queues.
- Constraint: strict per-user separation of data and processing.

## Requirements

### Bulk import

- The settings page accepts a file upload: plain text (UTF-8) with one URL per line; blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored; anything after the first whitespace on a line is ignored, so a line like `https://example.com some note` imports the URL alone. Any other file type (HTML, JSON, binary) is refused with "only plain-text files with one URL per line are accepted" and nothing is imported.
- Limits: file at most 2 MB and 5,000 URLs; over either, the upload is refused with "too large: at most 5,000 URLs / 2 MB per import" and nothing is imported.
- Processing: each line is normalised and added as in Adding links; the user sees a progress view with counts of added, duplicates (not added, not boosted) and invalid lines, the invalid lines listed with their line numbers, and a downloadable report. Imported links enter the stream with last used = import time, in file order (the first line of the file ends up highest), so a file sorted by the owner is honoured.
- Fetch and enrichment of imported links run in the background at no more than 20 links per minute per user (a 600-line import completes in about 30 minutes), and the stream updates as they complete. The same 20,000-link library limit applies; an import that would cross it stops at the limit and the report says so.
- The import is accepted via the API as well (`POST` of the file) with the same report returned as JSON.

### End-to-end flow

1. The owner uploads a 400-line text file; a progress view counts added/duplicates/invalid; the stream fills in over the following minutes; the report lists the 3 malformed lines.

## Design Decisions

1. **Bulk import is plain text only.** Owner's decision; the browser's HTML export is a later PRD. Imported links take the import time as last used, in file order, because a plain list carries no dates. (Source PRD decision 8.)
2. **Background processing is throttled to 20 links per minute per user** for imports, through package 03's shared throttle, which "enrich all" also uses; links pasted or added through the API one at a time are not throttled. Owner's decision on the rate (source PRD decision 15); the exemption for pasted links decided in this run, so that the 60-second goal for a pasted link holds during an import.
3. **The lines are added within the upload request; only fetching and enrichment are in the background.** The response, `201`, carries the full report. Decided in this run: 5,000 inserts fit one request in D1 batches, and the counts are then final when the progress view first appears.
4. **What counts as "another file type".** A file is refused as not plain text when its declared type (the request's `Content-Type`, or the multipart part's type) is neither `text/plain` nor absent, when it is not valid UTF-8, when it contains a NUL byte, or when its first non-blank characters are `<` (HTML, XML) or it parses as a JSON object or array. A UTF-8 byte-order mark is dropped, and `\r\n` and `\n` both end a line. Decided in this run: the source PRD names the types but not the test.
5. **The refusals' status codes**: 400 `unsupported_file` for another file type, 409 `import_too_large` for more than 2 MB (2,097,152 bytes) or more than 5,000 URL lines (lines that are neither blank nor comments), 400 `no_urls` for a file with no URL line. Decided in this run, following the API's rule that limits answer 409.
6. **A comment line** is one whose first non-whitespace character is `#`. Decided in this run.
7. **Duplicates** are lines whose normalised URL is already in the library or appeared on an earlier line of the file; the report lists each with its line number, and neither is boosted. Decided in this run; the source PRD makes them "not added, not boosted".
8. **Order within one import time**: line 1 gets the import time as last used and each later line one millisecond less, so that the stream's last-used order is the file order. Decided in this run, the same rule package 01 uses for a pasted batch.
9. **Two imports of the same user share the 20-per-minute budget**, dispatched in the order the imports were made; a link deleted before its turn is skipped without using the budget. Decided in this run.
10. **The report** is kept with the import and is available as JSON (`GET /api/v1/imports/{id}`) and as a downloadable text file (`GET /api/v1/imports/{id}/report`); the progress view polls the JSON every 5 seconds until every added link has left `pending`. Decided in this run.

## Dependencies

- Package 01 `accounts_links_and_stream`: `normalizeUrl`, the link store and its de-duplication, the library limit, the stream, the error envelope, the OpenAPI document, the Settings page and the shared test helpers.
- Package 02 `fetch_and_snapshot`: the fetch worker and `FETCH_QUEUE`, which imported links are dispatched to; the stream's in-place update; `e2e/fake-origin.ts`.
- Package 03 `ai_enrichment`: enrichment after fetch and the shared background throttle `src/worker/enrich/throttle.ts`; `e2e/fake-ai.ts`.

## Verified External API

None beyond the packages above: the work uses Hono 4.13.17 (request body and multipart parsing), D1 batches and the Queue binding that packages 01 and 02 set up, and the platform's `TextDecoder` with `fatal: true` to test UTF-8.

## Glossary

- **import**: one upload of a plain-text file of URLs, with its report.
- **URL line**: a line of the file that is neither blank nor a comment; its first whitespace-separated word is taken as the URL.
- **duplicate**: a URL line whose normalised URL is already in the library or on an earlier line of the same file.
- **report**: the counts of added, duplicate and invalid lines, the invalid and duplicate lines with their line numbers, and whether the library limit stopped the import.
- **throttle**: the per-user limit of 20 links per minute on background fetch and enrichment of imported links.
- **stream**: the home page listing, pinned links first then by last use descending.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Reading the import file

**Rationale:** The owner's list is whatever a text editor saved; it must be read the way a person reads it, and anything else refused before a single link is touched.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] THE import parser SHALL for any accepted file, drop a leading UTF-8 byte-order mark, split it into lines at '\n' or '\r\n', ignore blank lines and lines whose first non-whitespace character is '#', and take from every other line its first whitespace-separated word as the URL, numbering lines from 1 as they appear in the file
   → parseImportFile(bytes) returns {ok: true, lines: [{line: number, url: string}]}
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts, a table of (file text, expected [(line, url)]): ('https://a.example\nhttps://b.example', [(1, 'https://a.example'), (2, 'https://b.example')]); ('\uFEFFhttps://a.example\r\n\r\n# notes\r\n   # indented comment\r\nhttps://b.example some note here', [(1, 'https://a.example'), (5, 'https://b.example')]); ('  https://c.example\tx', [(1, 'https://c.example')]); ('https://d.example\n', [(1, 'https://d.example')]): assert parseImportFile(bytes) == {ok: true, lines: expected}
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF the uploaded file's declared type is neither text/plain nor absent, or its bytes are not valid UTF-8, contain a NUL byte, begin (after whitespace) with '<', or parse as a JSON object or array, THEN THE import parser SHALL refuse the upload, adding no link and recording no import
   → HTTP 400 with body {"error": "unsupported_file", "field": "file", "message": "only plain-text files with one URL per line are accepted"}; no link and no import is stored
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts, a table over uploads {Content-Type text/html with '<!doctype html><a href=...>'; text/plain with '<html><body>'; text/plain with '<?xml version="1.0"?>'; application/json with '["https://a.example"]'; text/plain with '{"urls": []}'; multipart part of type image/png; text/plain with bytes 0xC3 0x28 (invalid UTF-8); text/plain with a NUL byte}: r = api('POST', '/api/v1/imports', upload); assert r.status == 400 and r.json == {error: 'unsupported_file', field: 'file', message: 'only plain-text files with one URL per line are accepted'}; assert the link and import counts are unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF the uploaded file is larger than 2 MB (2,097,152 bytes) or holds more than 5,000 URL lines, THEN THE import parser SHALL refuse the upload, adding no link and recording no import
   → HTTP 409 with body {"error": "import_too_large", "message": "too large: at most 5,000 URLs / 2 MB per import"}; no link and no import is stored
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts, a table over files {2,097,153 bytes of comment lines and one URL; 5,001 distinct URL lines; 5,000 URL lines plus 300 comment lines and blank lines (accepted); exactly 2,097,152 bytes with fewer than 5,000 URLs (accepted)}: r = upload; for the refused rows assert r.status == 409 and r.json == {error: 'import_too_large', message: 'too large: at most 5,000 URLs / 2 MB per import'} and the link and import counts are unchanged; for the accepted rows assert r.status == 201
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF the uploaded file holds no URL line, or the request carries no file, THEN THE import parser SHALL refuse the upload, adding no link and recording no import
   → HTTP 400 with body {"error": "no_urls", "field": "file", "message": <text>}; no link and no import is stored
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts, a table over files {'', '\n\n', '# only a comment\n'} and a multipart request without a 'file' part: r = upload; assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error == 'no_urls' and r.json.field == 'file'; assert counts unchanged
   ```

### REQ-2: Adding the imported lines

**Rationale:** An import is the owner's list moved into the library as-is: every new URL added, nothing already there disturbed, every problem reported.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a user requests POST /api/v1/imports with a file the import parser accepts, THE Alexandria API SHALL normalise every URL line with the URL normaliser and store each new URL as a pending link with the URL word as its original URL and its host as provisional title, record the import with its report, and answer with the report
   → HTTP 201 with body {id, created_at, counts: {url_lines, added, duplicates, invalid, not_imported}, invalid: [{line, text}], duplicates: [{line, url}], stopped_at_limit: null | {line}}
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts, a table over the request forms {Content-Type text/plain with the file as body; multipart/form-data with the file in the part 'file'}: setNow(t); r = upload 'https://a.example/x?utm_source=y\nhttps://b.example'; assert r.status == 201 and r.json.counts == {url_lines: 2, added: 2, duplicates: 0, invalid: 0, not_imported: 0} and r.json.stopped_at_limit == null; assert the links have url 'https://a.example/x' (original_url with utm_source) and 'https://b.example', state 'pending', title the host; assert GET /api/v1/imports/{r.json.id} returns the same report
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF a URL line normalises to a URL already in the importing user's library or to the URL of an earlier line of the same file, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL report the line as a duplicate and neither add it nor boost the existing link
   → the line is listed in duplicates with its line number and normalised URL and counted in counts.duplicates; the existing link's last_used_at and use_count are unchanged
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts: the user has 'https://c.example' with last_used_at t0 and use_count 2; another user has 'https://d.example'; upload 'https://c.example/\nhttps://d.example\nhttps://D.example#x\nhttps://c.example?utm_medium=m'; assert counts.added == 1 (d.example for this user) and counts.duplicates == 3 and duplicates == [{line: 1, url: 'https://c.example'}, {line: 3, url: 'https://d.example'}, {line: 4, url: 'https://c.example'}]; assert c.example's last_used_at == t0 and use_count == 2
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] IF the URL normaliser rejects the URL of a line, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL report the line as invalid with its line number and text, and add nothing for it
   → the line is listed in invalid as {line, text} and counted in counts.invalid; no link is stored for it
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts: upload 'https://a.example\nnot-a-url\njavascript:alert(1)\nhttp://localhost/x\nhttps://b.example'; assert counts.invalid == 3 and invalid == [{line: 2, text: 'not-a-url'}, {line: 3, text: 'javascript:alert(1)'}, {line: 4, text: 'http://localhost/x'}] and counts.added == 2
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] WHEN an import adds links, THE Alexandria API SHALL give the added links last-used times from the import time downwards in file order, one millisecond apart, so that the stream lists them in file order with the first line highest, above every link last used before the import
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts: seed an older link used at t - 1 day; setNow(t); upload 'https://z.example\nhttps://a.example\nhttps://m.example'; assert the added links' last_used_at == [t, t - 1 ms, t - 2 ms] and added_at == t; assert GET /api/v1/links lists z, a, m, then the older link
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] IF adding the next new URL of an import would take the user's library past 20,000 links, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL stop adding at the limit, leave every later line unprocessed, and say in the report on which line the import stopped
   → HTTP 201 with the report; stopped_at_limit is {line: <the first line not imported>}; counts.not_imported counts that line and every later URL line; the library holds 20,000 links
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts: seed the user with 19,998 links; upload 5 new URL lines with a duplicate on line 2; assert r.status == 201, counts == {url_lines: 5, added: 2, duplicates: 1, invalid: 0, not_imported: 2} and stopped_at_limit == {line: 4}; assert the library holds 20,000 links; and with 20,000 links already, an upload adds none and stops at its first new URL line
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] THE Alexandria API SHALL for any accepted file, account for every URL line exactly once: counts.added + counts.duplicates + counts.invalid + counts.not_imported equals counts.url_lines, and the user's link count grows by counts.added
   → the report's counts satisfy added + duplicates + invalid + not_imported == url_lines
   Check: property
   ```
   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts: for 50 generated files of 1 to 300 lines mixing new URLs, URLs already in the library, repeated URLs with different case, fragments and tracking parameters, invalid inputs, comments and blank lines, against libraries seeded near and far from the limit: r = upload; assert the sum of the four counts == counts.url_lines and links after == links before + counts.added
   ```

### REQ-3: Throttled background processing

**Rationale:** An import is a flood; fetching and enriching it slowly keeps the provider calls, the owner's AI bill and the origins' load low.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] THE import dispatcher SHALL for any import, send its added links to the fetch worker in file order, at most 20 links per minute per user through the shared background throttle, so that each is fetched and then enriched as any added link is
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts with the clock set through setNow and the fetch queue captured: upload 45 new URLs at t; run the dispatcher at t, t + 30 s, t + 60 s, t + 120 s; assert the captured fetch messages are the links of lines 1-20 by t + 59 s, 21-40 by t + 119 s and 41-45 by t + 120 s, in line order, and never more than 20 in any 60-second window
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] THE import dispatcher SHALL for any user with several imports, and with 'enrich all unenriched links' running, share one budget of 20 links per minute between them, dispatching earlier imports' links first, while another user's imports keep a budget of their own
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts, a table over {user A imports 15 and then 15 more; user A imports 15 while 'enrich all' has 15 waiting; users A and B import 20 each}: run the dispatcher for one minute of clock time; assert A receives at most 20 dispatches in that minute, the first import's links before the second's, and B receives its 20 regardless of A
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] IF an imported link waiting for its turn has been deleted, or has already been sent to the fetch worker by another action such as a refresh, THEN THE import dispatcher SHALL skip the link without sending it to the fetch worker and without using the budget, so that the next link takes its slot
   → no fetch message for that link; the minute's 20 slots go to the next waiting links
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts: upload 21 new URLs; delete the link of line 3 and refresh the link of line 4 through POST /api/v1/links/{id}/refresh before the dispatcher runs; run it once; assert the dispatched links are exactly those of lines 1, 2 and 5-21 in that order, with no fetch message for line 3 and only the refresh's message for line 4; then upload 25 more and delete their line 1 before the next minute's run, and assert that run dispatches their lines 2-21 (20 links)
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] THE import dispatcher SHALL for any link added by a paste or by POST /api/v1/links while an import is waiting, send it to the fetch worker at once, outside the import's budget
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts: upload 100 new URLs; immediately POST /api/v1/links 'https://pasted.example'; assert a fetch message for the pasted link is sent before the dispatcher's next run and the import's dispatches in that minute are still 20
   ```

### REQ-4: Import progress and report

**Rationale:** An import that runs for half an hour needs a way to see where it is and what it refused.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN a user requests GET /api/v1/imports/{id} for one of their imports, THE Alexandria API SHALL return the import's report and its progress: how many added links are still waiting for their turn, how many have been sent and are still pending, and how many have left pending, of which how many are enriched
   → HTTP 200 with body {<the report of POST /api/v1/imports>, progress: {waiting, in_progress, done, enriched}}
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts: upload 30 new URLs; dispatch 20; complete the fetch of 5 with the fetch worker against a local origin double and enrich 3 of them with the provider double; r = api('GET', '/api/v1/imports/' + id); assert r.json.counts.added == 30 and r.json.progress == {waiting: 10, in_progress: 15, done: 5, enriched: 3}
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN a user requests GET /api/v1/imports/{id}/report for one of their imports, THE Alexandria API SHALL return the report as a downloadable plain-text file listing the import date, the counts, every invalid line with its number and text, every duplicate with its line number and URL, and the line where the library limit stopped the import, when it did
   → HTTP 200, Content-Type text/plain; charset=utf-8, Content-Disposition attachment with filename alexandria-import-<YYYY-MM-DD>.txt
   Check: unit
   ```

1. [REQ-4.3] IF the import id names no import of the authenticated user, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL answer as for a resource that does not exist
   → HTTP 404 with body {"error": "not_found"}

   in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts, a table over {GET /api/v1/imports/{B's id}, GET /api/v1/imports/{B's id}/report, an id that exists nowhere} as user A: assert status 404 and body {error: 'not_found'}
   ```

1. [REQ-5.3] WHEN the report says the library limit stopped the import, THE website SHALL show the import's stopping line when the library limit stopped it

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: The owner imports a 400-line file and the stream fills in

1. **owner** chooses a 400-line text file with 397 URLs and 3 malformed lines in the settings page's Import section and starts the import
2. **website** uploads the file with POST /api/v1/imports
3. **Alexandria API** parses the file, adds 397 pending links with last-used times in file order, records the import and answers with the report
4. **website** shows the progress view: added 397, duplicates 0, invalid 3, the three malformed lines with their numbers
5. **Alexandria API** dispatches the imported links to the fetch queue, 20 in the first minute, in file order
6. **fetch worker** fetches and snapshots the dispatched pages and moves each link out of pending
7. **enrichment worker** enriches each fetched link with the owner's AI key
8. **AI provider** answers each enrichment request with a summary, tags and a topic
9. **owner** sees the stream list the imported links in file order, the first ones titled and summarised, and downloads the report listing the 3 malformed lines

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** website, Alexandria API, D1 database, Queues, fetch worker, enrichment worker, the shared background throttle

**Setup:**

- wrangler dev with local D1, R2 and Queues, the owner signed in through e2e/fake-google.ts with an AI key pointing at e2e/fake-ai.ts
- e2e/fake-origin.ts serves the 397 imported URLs as distinct pages (the external parties are the only stubs)
- a 400-line UTF-8 file with 397 URLs on hosts of e2e/fake-origin.ts and 3 malformed lines at 57, 211 and 399

**End state:**

- the import report has counts {url_lines: 400, added: 397, duplicates: 0, invalid: 3, not_imported: 0} and invalid lines 57, 211 and 399
- the stream's first 397 links follow the file's order
- after 70 seconds between 1 and 20 imported links have left pending, and at no moment have more than 20 been dispatched in a 60-second window
- the downloaded report lists the three malformed lines with their numbers

**Pseudocode:**

```
in e2e/import.spec.ts: sign in; on /settings set the file input and click 'Import'; expect 'added 397', 'invalid 3' and the three line rows; read the stream through GET /api/v1/links and expect its hosts in file order; wait 70 s; expect 1 <= links not pending <= 20 and the first stream card titled from its page; download the report and expect 'line 57', 'line 211', 'line 399'
```

## Dependencies

- `01` — reuses normalizeUrl, the link store, the 20,000-link limit, the stream order, the error envelope, the OpenAPI document and the Settings page
- `02` — imported links are fetched and snapshotted by the fetch worker through FETCH_QUEUE
- `03` — imported links are enriched after fetch and dispatched through the shared 20-per-minute background throttle

## Tasks

### 1. Accept an import file and add its lines to the library (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1, REQ-2

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the parsing, refusal and adding behaviours to src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts and confirm they fail
- 1.2 Write parseImportFile in src/worker/imports/parse.ts: refuse a declared type other than text/plain, bytes that are not valid UTF-8 (TextDecoder with fatal), a NUL byte, a first non-blank '<', and a body that parses as a JSON object or array; drop a byte-order mark; split on '\n' and '\r\n'; ignore blank and '#' lines; take each remaining line's first whitespace-separated word with its 1-based line number
- 1.3 Implement POST /api/v1/imports in src/worker/imports/routes.ts for a text/plain body and for multipart/form-data with the part 'file': 400 unsupported_file, 409 import_too_large over 2,097,152 bytes or 5,000 URL lines, 400 no_urls, each with its exact message and nothing stored
- 1.4 Add a migration with the imports table (id, user, created time, counts, invalid and duplicate lines, stopped line) and the import_links table (import, link, line, dispatched time)
- 1.5 Write importLines in src/worker/imports/imports.ts: normalise each line with normalizeUrl; list invalid lines; treat a URL already in the library or seen on an earlier line as a duplicate, without boosting; insert the new links pending, last used from the import time downwards one millisecond per line, in D1 batches, without sending them to the fetch queue; stop at the 20,000-link limit and record the stopping line
- 1.6 Answer 201 with the report {id, created_at, counts, invalid, duplicates, stopped_at_limit}
- 1.7 Document the route in the OpenAPI document and docs/api.md

### 2. Dispatch imported links to the fetch worker through the shared throttle (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the dispatch behaviours to src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts and confirm they fail
- 2.2 Hand each import's links, in line order, to the shared background throttle in src/worker/enrich/throttle.ts, which releases at most 20 links per minute per user across imports and 'enrich all', earlier work first, and sends each released link to the fetch queue

- 2.4 Keep links added by paste or POST /api/v1/links going straight to the fetch queue, outside the throttle
